Ready meals for the chiller aisle in every store across the city.
Party trays for weddings, conferences, schools and hospital canteens.
Frozen egusi and amala packs trucked cold to shops in other states.
Cold trucks cross the border. Yes, they are buying Nigerian jollof.
Containers of frozen meals for homesick Nigerians in the diaspora.

milestones.title: Second Pot on the Fire
milestones.blurb: Your first branch opens in Lagos. The recipe must now taste the same in two places.

milestones.title: Five Kitchens, One Taste
milestones.blurb: Recipe cards and measured spice mixes keep every pot of jollof the same.

milestones.title: Central Kitchen Opens
milestones.blurb: One big kitchen now preps stew base and soups for all the Lagos branches.

milestones.title: Lagos Lunch Champion
milestones.blurb: Offices across the city order daily. Bulk buying of rice and beef cuts your costs.

milestones.title: Beyond Lagos
milestones.blurb: Branches in other states. Local farmers now supply yam, pepper and palm oil directly.

milestones.title: A Household Name
milestones.blurb: One hundred kitchens. Travellers know they can find your egusi in any big city.

milestones.title: West Africa Is Eating
milestones.blurb: Kitchens open along the coast. The jollof debate now happens inside your shop.

milestones.title: Cooking School Founded
milestones.blurb: Your own academy trains cooks and managers, so new branches open faster.

milestones.title: Kitchens Overseas
milestones.blurb: Diaspora cities queue for amala and pounded yam that tastes like home.

milestones.title: The World's Nigerian Kitchen
milestones.blurb: Five hundred kitchens on three continents, all from one pot by the roadside.

events.text: Power is steady and the blenders never stop. The kitchen is flying!

research.claim: A Nigerian quick-service group has grown its local-food restaurant brand state by state, opening a Kaduna branch to target the northern market.
A Lagos casual food chain reached its 12th location in late 2024, showing how city chains grow outlet by outlet before leaving Lagos.
Entrepreneurs are selling frozen, ready-to-heat West African meals such as jollof through grocery stores in the United States.
Catering for owambe events (weddings and large parties) is a recognised route for Nigerian cooks to scale into bulk food production.
